title: The Fox Who Had Lost His Tail
author: Aesop (adapted by J. H. Stickney)
summary: 断尾狐狸劝同伴都舍弃尾巴，被老狐狸当众拆穿。
publicDomainBasis: Aesop's fables are ancient; this retelling by J. H. Stickney was published in 1915. Published before 1923 and therefore public domain in the United States; Project Gutenberg releases it as public domain.

paragraphs.en: A FOX was once caught in a trap by his tail. He succeeded in getting away, but was forced to leave his “brush” behind. He soon realized that his life would be a burden, from the shame and ridicule to which his tailless condition would expose him.
paragraphs.zh: 有一次，一只狐狸的尾巴被夹子夹住了。他设法逃了出来，却不得不把那条“大尾巴”留在了夹子上。他很快意识到，没了尾巴，他会招来羞辱和嘲笑，日子将变得苦不堪言。

paragraphs.en: “I must not own that it is a misfortune not to have a bushy tail,” he said to himself.
paragraphs.zh: “我绝不能承认没有蓬松尾巴是件倒霉事。”他对自己说。

paragraphs.en: So he set about to induce all the other Foxes to part with theirs. At the next assembly he boldly made a speech, in which he set forth the advantages of his present state.
paragraphs.zh: 于是他想方设法劝别的狐狸都舍弃尾巴。下一次聚会上，他大胆地发表了一通演说，大讲自己如今这状态的好处。

paragraphs.en: “The tail,” he said, “is no real part of our persons, and besides being very ugly to see, it exposes us to danger from the dogs. I have never moved about with such ease as since I gave up my own.”
paragraphs.zh: “尾巴，”他说，“根本不是我们身上真正的一部分，而且除了难看，还会让我们遭到狗的危险。自从我舍掉自己的尾巴，行动起来从没这么轻便过。”

paragraphs.en: When he had ended his speech, a sly old Fox arose, and giving his own brush a graceful wave, said, with the kind of sneer which all Foxes know so well how to give, that if he had lost by accident his own tail, he should, without doubt, agree with his friend; but that, as the brush was a fox’s chief ornament and distinction, until such a mishap should occur as had befallen his friend, he should retain his own and should advise the others to do the same. And the vote to retain the tails was given by a wave of the brush. Yet many fashions have been set by Foxes who have met with some such accident.
paragraphs.zh: 他话音刚落，一只狡猾的老狐狸站起来，优雅地甩了甩自己的大尾巴，用狐狸们最擅长的那种讥笑口气说：如果他是意外丢了自己的尾巴，那他无疑会赞同这位朋友的话；可既然尾巴是狐狸最主要的装饰和标志，在遭遇这位朋友那样的不幸之前，他还是要保留自己的尾巴，也劝大家照样保留。于是，保留尾巴的决议就在一片甩尾巴的动作中通过了。不过，许多时髦风气，正是由遭遇这类意外的狐狸带起来的。
